subject: Really simple qplot fails to display correctly

messages.author: 91149ba1c4919e8b
messages.subject: Really simple qplot fails to display correctly
parts:
Dear All,
anyone would know why this really simple qplot fails to display correctly? In particular, the vertical axis in incomplete.

Here the code to reproduce the issue:

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
data <- data.frame(rbind( c("Product_1", "Q1", 100L ), c("Product_2", "Q1", 200L), c("Product_1", "Q2", 120L), c("Product_2", "Q2", 220L)))
names(data) <- c("Product", "Quarter", "Quantity")
data.melt <- melt(data, id=c("Product", "Quarter"), measure="Quantity")
qplot(data=data.melt, x=Quarter, y=value, fill=Product, geom="bar", stat="identity")

I created this case while investigating another more complex one, in which ggplot2 doesn't sum up as expected all values that belong to the same bar. I will probably post later about it, once I have been able to do some more tests.

Thanks!

Best Regards,
Marco.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Really simple qplot fails to display correctly
parts:
Hi:

You can start here to identify the problem: notice the class of Quantity.

> data <- data.frame(rbind( c("Product_1", "Q1", 100L ), c("Product_2", "Q1", 200L), c("Product_1", "Q2", 120L), c("Product_2", "Q2", 220L)))
> names(data) <- c("Product", "Quarter", "Quantity")

> str(data)
'data.frame':   4 obs. of  3 variables:
 $ Product : Factor w/ 2 levels "Product_1","Product_2": 1 2 1 2
 $ Quarter : Factor w/ 2 levels "Q1","Q2": 1 1 2 2
 $ Quantity: Factor w/ 4 levels "100","120","200",..: 1 3 2 4

...and it doesn't get fixed by reshaping:

> data.melt <- reshape2::melt(data, id=c("Product", "Quarter"), measure="Quantity")
> str(data.melt)
'data.frame':   4 obs. of  4 variables:
 $ Product : Factor w/ 2 levels "Product_1","Product_2": 1 2 1 2
 $ Quarter : Factor w/ 2 levels "Q1","Q2": 1 1 2 2
 $ variable: Factor w/ 1 level "Quantity": 1 1 1 1
 $ value   : chr  "100" "200" "120" "220"

Hint: Don't use rbind() or cbind() to create data frames; both produce matrices before being converted to data frames, and matrices can only be of one data type. When you mix different classes of objects in a matrix, R coerces the type to the simplest one that all elements can fulfill. In this case, the common type is factor.

So:
(1) This is not a ggplot2 problem, it's a data frame construction problem.
(2) When you fix the data frame definition, the qplot() call will work.
(3) data() and df() are common function names in R, so please use a more imaginative name for your data object.

Fixup:

dat <- data.frame(Product = factor(rep(c("Product_1", "Product_2"), 2)),
                          Quarter = factor(rep(c("Q1", "Q2"), each = 2)),
                          Quantity = c(100, 200, 120, 220))
library(reshape2)
dat.melt <- melt(dat, id = c("Product", "Quarter"))
library(ggplot2)
qplot(data=dat.melt, x=Quarter, y=value, fill=Product, geom="bar", stat="identity")

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Really simple qplot fails to display correctly
parts:
Dear Dennis,
thank you very much for your quick and detailed explanation, which indeed makes a lot of sense to me.

I would have expected ggplot2 to issue at least a warning when asked to stack factors. In my original (dumb) example, apparently such factors are "summed up" correctly for Q1, but not for Q2, leading to the visualization issue. No warning whatsoever is issued, which indeed doesn't suggest that the problem may lay in the dataset as it actually does. Confusing at least.

Is there a use case where stacking factors in a bar chart would indeed be appropriate and should not issue a warning?

Best Regards,
Marco.
